title: Precision Mode Ledger: lightweight session fidelity lanes
content:
Context:
Small personal deep-dive — trying to capture a compact design for an opt-in 'Precision Mode' that gives clients deterministic/finer-grained fidelity controls per session. Goal is a tiny surface to let product teams trade quality for cost/latency without shipping whole pricing tiers.

Problem statement:
- Teams need predictable per-session unit economics. Today we have global quantization/batching suggestions but no per-session contract.
- Apps with mixed use (short facts + long creative) want to route important sessions to high-fidelity and noisy ones to cheaper lanes.
- Ops wants simple signals to enforce SLOs and measure impact.

High level idea:
- Introduce 3 simple session lanes: precision, balanced, frugal. Each lane configures: model variant (full/quantized), max tokens per response, KV cache retention policy, and batching priority.
- Sessions get labeled at creation by caller or heuristic. Platform uses labels for routing and cost accounting.

Success metrics (initial):
- 10% reduction in average token cost for mixed workloads (pilot customers)
- <2% regression in user-facing quality for frugal lane measured by L0 eval set
- Adoption: 3 pilot customers enabling session lanes for 6+ weeks

Personas:
- Growth PM: wants a cheap way to add tiered responses in product experiments
- Platform engineer (customer): expects predictable billing and easy opt-in/out
- SRE: needs clear routing semantics to debug fallbacks

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I can mark a session as "precision" at creation so subsequent calls use full-fidelity path.
- As a platform admin, I can define per-customer defaults (default lane, overrides).
- As an app, I can request a switch mid-session (e.g., escalate to precision when user pays).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: session.create(session_id, lane="precision|balanced|frugal") accepted and persisted
- Runtime: requests annotated by session_id respect lane selection (model variant + batch priority)
- Billing: cost breakdown shows tokens consumed per lane for customer invoice
- Observability: per-lane latency and token rate dashboard + one error alert

Implementation sketch:
- Storage: session metadata record with lane, last_modified, override_count (cheap)
- Router: small heuristic layer maps lane->execution config (model, quant, batch queue, cache ttl)
- Billing: add lane tag to token-usage record so Analytics can sum per-lane

API proto (example snippets):
- Create session
  POST /v1/sessions
  {
    "session_id": "sess_abc123",
    "lane": "frugal",
    "metadata": {"experiment": "reduced-cost-A"}
  }
- Switch lane mid-session
  POST /v1/sessions/sess_abc123/lane
  {"lane": "precision"}

UX notes:
- Make lane visible in Console with quick toggle and short tooltip: "Precision: higher cost, lower latency variance, full context"
- Exposure: hide advanced lanes by default for new customers; part of feature flag rollout

Experiment plan (pilot):
- Week 0: internal sandbox with 2 internal apps (support, docs bot)
- Week 1–3: 2 paid customers opt-in for split traffic A/B: default vs. lane-aware routing
- Measure cost delta, latency P95/P99, and micro-eval quality on a tiny prompt set

Risks & open questions:
- QoS guarantees: can we ensure precision lane actually avoids falling back to frugal under load? (need routing preemption rules)
- Complexity: how many lanes before customers confused? start with three; add custom later
- Billing disputes: customers will question per-lane pricing — require clear invoicing and bill-explainability

Dependencies:
- Router + model variant mapping (eng-serving-runtime)
- Billing pipeline change to tag lane (finance infra)
- Console toggle in product-ui (console-and-rollouts)

Next steps (for me):
- Sync w/ Mira and Ben on 11/09 to align on router signal semantics
- Draft a 1-page proposal for pilot customers (include pricing hypothesis)
- Quick proto in internal sandbox; aim for an internal demo by 11/30

Notes to self:
- Keep API surface minimal. No mandatory billing changes for MVP; just capture lane tags and show analytics.
- Consider default heuristics: short session length -> frugal; high edit rate -> precision? need data.
- Save short prompt set for micro-eval (10 prompts per lane)

TODOs:
- [ ] write pilot pricing memo
- [ ] small tracing experiment to ensure lane propagation across services
- [ ] update docs with example SDK calls

-- end of ledger (working, intentionally terse)
